newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends mostly higher, but well off peaks.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends mostly higher, but well off peaks.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended mainly higher on Monday, but profit-taking by day traders and steady producer selling knocked prices off peaks, dealers said.
Benchmark July coffee leapt to a intraday high of 224.50 cents per lb -- just short of resistance at 225.00 cents, its life-of-contract high set Friday -- before ending at 218.50, up 2.35 on the day.
Spot May rose 3.35 cents, to 250.90, while the back months closed 3.00 higher to 0.10 lower.
After a mixed opening, prices climbed sharply this morning on local and speculative buying after news of a warehouse fire in Costa Rica re-ignited supply worries.
"The news from Costa Rica certainly forced some new buying," said one trader. "But once it was disseminated, the market came off."
A spokesman for Costa Rican Fedecoop (Federacin de Cooperativas de Caficultores) said on Monday the fire destroyed an unquantified amount of coffee and damaged the warehouse where it was stored.

"Although we have not been able to quantify the damage, neither the buildings nor the amount of coffee destroyed, we can say that the coffee losses are much less than the 50,000 bags being talked about," Luis Diego Snchez, Fedecoop manager told Reuters.
While the losses in Costa Rica may come in well below 50,000 bags, traders said any supply problems at a time when inventories were already at low levels are percieved as bullish.
"It doesn't take much to get this market going," one trader said. "And most of the run today was attributed to the warehouse fire in Costa Rica."
Low consumer stocks have seen the nearby spreads become sharply backwardated, with the CSCE May/July spread widening to 31.40 cents today from 30.40 at the close on Friday.

Traders continued to closely monitor stockpiles of coffee for delivery against the exchange. After Friday's close, the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 750 bags, to 42,918 bags -- the equivalent of about 152 lots -- as of May 1. Meanwhile, open interest on the May contract, which expires in two weeks, was still relatively high at 1,276 lots.
However, the CSCE also reported after the Friday's close that there were 10,477 bags of coffee pending grading.

Technically, traders pegged near-term resistance at 220.00, with a strong upside hurdle noted at 225.00, its lifeime high. Support was seen at 212.00 basis July, with a breach of that level expected to lead to a test of the psychologically crucial $2 mark.
LIFFE coffee market in London was closed on Monday for a bank holiday and will reopen on Tuesday.
